category_title: Students who exhibit initial fear and avoidance but transition to engagement through curiosity and hands-on success
student_description: This student experiences intense fear and physical avoidance of novel biological specimens (e.g., bugs, worms) but possesses a strong underlying curiosity and a desire to be a scientist. They uniquely require playful social validation, humor, and conversational scaffolding to self-regulate, overcome their anxiety, and transform their fear into pride.

criteria.rationale: This student relies heavily on social interaction and group dynamics to gradually build openness to novel, frightening biological tasks over time.
criteria.check: The long-term plan includes organizing group work or peer-based social interactions around hands-on activities to support gradual exposure to feared stimuli.

criteria.rationale: By designing environments that support their developing interest, the student learns to use their own self-regulation tactics (like self-talk and countdowns) to satisfy their curiosity.
criteria.check: The long-term plan outlines a gradual release of external support, providing scaffolding initially while encouraging the student to use and refine their own self-regulation strategies during hands-on tasks.
